items.title: For investors with patience and ability to take moderate risk: 5 mid-cap stocks with upside potential of up to 26%
items.description: For all those who have decided it is now time to turn bullish, here’s a small reminder: The past year has been a very tough one for mid-cap stocks. So, if this is the segment you are interested in, be calm and be prepared. Because panic and anxiety during a correction are the worst things for any investor with high exposure to mid-cap stocks.

items.title: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide D-Street action on Monday
items.description: Indian equities snapped their recent rally as retail inflation breached the RBI’s upper tolerance limit, triggering caution among investors. Analysts expect near-term consolidation with a positive bias, while Nvidia’s results and US Fed minutes remain key global triggers.

items.title: Time for a contrarian and tactical look? 7 stocks from the real estate sector with upside potential ranging from 9% to 43%
items.description: Despite taking many blows in the last two years, including a war, the Indian economy has fared better than most expected. That is the kind of resilience worth keeping in mind when looking at a sector the market gave up on long ago. Here’s why real estate may deserve a tactical place on a watchlist, for those who can carry the risk. Stock Reports Plus, powered by Refinitiv, is a comprehensive report that evaluates five key components of 4,000+ listed stocks – earnings, fundamentals, relative valuation, risk, and price momentum – to generate standardised scores. The simple average of the above-mentioned five component ratings is normally distributed to reach an average score.

items.title: 11 penny stocks plunge up to 84% in six months. Do you own any?
items.description: Over the past six months, 11 penny stocks have corrected sharply, falling between 50% and 84%. These stocks were identified through a screen of companies with a market capitalisation of less than Rs 1,000 crore, a share price below Rs 20 and a minimum recent trading volume of 5 lakh shares. The screen captures low-priced, relatively liquid penny stocks that have witnessed significant price declines during the period. (Data Source: ACE Equi).

items.title: FIIs buy record Rs 84,000 crore in Indian stocks this month, but there are two warning signs
items.description: Foreign investors have poured over Rs 84,000 crore into Indian equities in the first two weeks of November, reversing months of heavy selling. Improving earnings, lower crude prices and a shift in global investment preferences have supported the return, but inflation and geopolitical risks remain concerns.

items.title: Two Trades for Today: A leading sugar producer for a 6.4% upmove, a small-cap IT stock for a gain of about 6%
items.description: Our technical analysts identify select stocks every trading day that may gain momentum even in volatile markets. Here are the technical calls for today.

items.title: Sebi to issue AI usage guidelines for capital markets, focus on investor protection: Tuhin Kanta Pandey
items.description: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) is set to release new guidelines aimed at promoting the responsible use of Artificial Intelligence within capital markets. The primary objectives include ensuring investor protection and establishing accountability across regulated entities. Additionally, a working group has been initiated to bolster the Innovators Growth Platform for startups.

items.title: FPIs pump Rs 84,290 crore into D-Street in first fortnight of November
items.description: Foreign Portfolio Investors made substantial investments in Indian equities during the first half of November. This influx followed two months of significant capital outflows amidst global market shifts. Falling crude prices and attractive valuations in large-cap stocks contributed to this turnaround. The benchmark Nifty index benefited from this resurgence, surpassing the 25,000 mark as key sectors rallied.

items.title: AI retreat fuels India stock comeback in great rotation trade
items.description: Indian stocks are staging a strong comeback as global investors rotate away from crowded AI bets towards markets with improving earnings and attractive valuations. Falling oil prices and renewed foreign inflows are further supporting the recovery.

items.title: Stock splits & dividends: Oil India, Cochin Shipyard, MRF among 31 companies  turning ex-record date this week
items.description: This week promises excitement for investors with 31 companies, including Cochin Shipyard and Oil India, marking their ex-record dates. Notable dividend announcements include the Shipping Corporation of India and MRF set for November 16. Power Finance Corporation and Page Industries will declare their dividends on November 17 and 18 respectively, while Oil India will finalize interim dividends on November 20. Shareholders must possess shares before these record dates to qualify.

items.title: Will Sensex, Nifty continue their bull run or consolidate? 4 factors to watch out for this week
items.description: The Sensex and Nifty have seen minor fluctuations recently due to profit-taking after a remarkable surge. Notably, Foreign Institutional Investors continue to show robust engagement in Indian markets, being net buyers for the last ten sessions. Meanwhile, oil prices are experiencing instability fueled by ongoing geopolitical issues in the Middle East, while inflation concerns are driving speculation around potential interest rate increases by the Reserve Bank of India.
